name: Insulated-gate MOS transistor
summary: A silicon transistor whose current is switched by a metal gate separated from the silicon by a thin oxide layer, a design later taken up for integrated circuits.
description: Atalla and Kahng demonstrated a silicon field-effect transistor with an oxide-insulated gate controlling conduction between source and drain.
tier_reason: The insulated-gate transistor architecture underlies subsequent MOS integration and computing across device generations.

impact.note: The MOS transistor is in nearly every chip most of humanity now carries or relies on, and unrelated fields stand on it as a platform.

why: Atalla's thermally grown oxide had just been shown to stabilise silicon surfaces, making an insulated-gate field-effect device practical.

places.note: String names only New Jersey; Murray Hill assumed as Bell Labs' main site

date.basis: Museum narrative dates successful fabrication to 1959; the 1960 meeting report is corroborated by Moore’s account.
